source.title: FORMAT(X, D) takes D modulo 2^32: FORMAT(1.5, 4294967298) = '1.50' and FORMAT(1.5, 2147483648) = '2'

header.Bug #121511: FORMAT(X, D) takes D modulo 2^32: FORMAT(1.5, 4294967298) = '1.50' and FORMAT(1.5, 2147483648) = '2'

comments.author: Ke Han
comments.text:
Description:
FORMAT(X, D) clamps a large D to the maximum number of decimals (30): both
FORMAT(1.5, 40) and FORMAT(1.5, 2147483647) return 1.5 with 30 decimals.
But D is first cast to int, so a D of 2^31 or more is taken modulo 2^32:

  - D = 4294967298 (2^32 + 2) formats with 2 decimals: '1.50';
  - D = 2147483648 (2^31) becomes negative and formats with 0 decimals: '2';
  - D = 4294967336 (2^32 + 40) is clamped to 30 only because 40 > 30;
  - the same happens with a BIGINT column as D, and with the 3-argument
    form FORMAT(X, D, locale).

No warning is given.  ROUND() and TRUNCATE(), which also take a decimals
argument, were fixed for huge D by Bug #24912: ROUND(1.5, 4294967298) is 1.5.

Cause: sql/item_strfunc.cc, Item_func_format::val_str_ascii(), trunk 3b99be40:

    int dec = (int)args[1]->val_int();
    ...
    dec = set_zone(dec, 0, FORMAT_MAX_DECIMALS);

The (int) cast keeps the low 32 bits before set_zone() clamps to 0..30.

How to repeat:
SELECT FORMAT(1.5, 2) AS d2, FORMAT(1.5, 4294967298) AS d2p32_2,
       FORMAT(1.5, 2147483648) AS d2p31, FORMAT(1.5, -1) AS dm1;
+------+---------+-------+------+
| d2   | d2p32_2 | d2p31 | dm1  |
+------+---------+-------+------+
| 1.50 | 1.50    | 2     | 2    |
+------+---------+-------+------+

SELECT LENGTH(FORMAT(1.5, 40)) AS len_d40,
       LENGTH(FORMAT(1.5, 2147483647)) AS len_d2p31m1;
+---------+-------------+
| len_d40 | len_d2p31m1 |
+---------+-------------+
|      32 |          32 |
+---------+-------------+

SELECT FORMAT(1234567.891, 4294967297, 'de_DE') AS de_d2p32_1,
       FORMAT(1234567.891, 1, 'de_DE') AS de_d1;
+-------------+-------------+
| de_d2p32_1  | de_d1       |
+-------------+-------------+
| 1.234.567,9 | 1.234.567,9 |
+-------------+-------------+

SELECT ROUND(1.5, 4294967298) AS round_d2p32_2, TRUNCATE(1.5, 4294967298) AS trunc_d2p32_2;
+---------------+---------------+
| round_d2p32_2 | trunc_d2p32_2 |
+---------------+---------------+
|           1.5 |           1.5 |
+---------------+---------------+

CREATE TABLE t016 (d BIGINT);
INSERT INTO t016 VALUES (2), (4294967298), (2147483648);
SELECT d, FORMAT(1.5, d) AS f FROM t016 ORDER BY d;
+------------+------+
| d          | f    |
+------------+------+
|          2 | 1.50 |
| 2147483648 | 2    |
| 4294967298 | 1.50 |
+------------+------+

Expected: any D above 30 gives 30 decimals, as for D = 40 and D =
2147483647.  FORMAT(1.5, 4294967298) and FORMAT(1.5, 2147483648) should
both be '1.500000000000000000000000000000'.

Suggested fix:
Clamp before narrowing, e.g.

    const longlong d = args[1]->val_int();
    int dec = (d < 0 && !args[1]->unsigned_flag) ? 0
            : (d > FORMAT_MAX_DECIMALS || (d < 0 && args[1]->unsigned_flag))
                  ? FORMAT_MAX_DECIMALS : static_cast<int>(d);

(the unsigned_flag check keeps D >= 2^63 from being read as negative).
